primaryGround: LOC Mass Deacidification Program; Selection lines 62–88; Quality Controls 93–102. Most Bookkeeper candidate volumes are structurally sound; softbound volumes must be sound and not too brittle, and binding adhesive must support the text. Plasticized covers do not fully absorb MgO. LOC states the process uses magnesium oxide (MgO) to neutralize paper acids; the process takes 1½ hours and raises pH to 6.8–10.4, achieves a 1–3% alkaline reserve, and extends useful life by over 300%. Surrogate test papers are included in 10% of batches, with a mass-based MgO check.

LOC Copper-Catalyzed Degradation of Paper; Lines 11–19. A Barrow two-step treatment used calcium hydroxide and calcium bicarbonate. LOC discusses it as an aqueous deacidification treatment distinct from Bookkeeper. Other tested aqueous deacidification agents included magnesium bicarbonate and zinc bicarbonate; the study also describes sodium bicarbonate neutralization followed by washing.

NPS Conserve O Gram 13/3: Polyester Encapsulation; Page 1, lines 3–55. Encapsulation sandwiches a paper object between two stiff, chemically inert, clear plastic sheets; all edges are sealed. It supports and protects fragile papers, and supports documents handled during research where both sides need visibility. Removing a four-edge encapsulation requires cutting it open; U- and L-seals permit extraction without destroying the enclosure but provide less protection. Electrostatic charge can damage charcoal, pastel and flaking watercolor. Buffering acidic paper before permanent encapsulation is recommended; magnesium or calcium carbonate neutralizes existing acid and leaves a reserve.

LOC Action Plan: Mass Deacidification; Lines 33–49. Under Phase A, LOC pursued refinement of the diethyl zinc (DEZ) process. Phase B enabled evaluation of other promising technologies; Preservation Technologies asked LOC to evaluate Bookkeeper. LOC did not request Congressional support for DEZ because of projected high capitalization costs and encouraging Bookkeeper developments. The appointed team studied Bookkeeper as a distinct process.

literal.prompt: По руководству NPS о расправлении свёрнутой бумаги какой метод требует дополнительной экспертизы и профессионального консерватора, если на листе есть железо-галловые чернила?

primaryGround: NPS Conserve O Gram 13/2: Flatten Folded or Rolled Paper; Introduction/cautions lines 24–38. Objects with iron gall ink require additional expertise and should only be treated by a professional conservator.

explanation.literal: Увлажнение в протоколе NPS расслабляет свёрнутую бумагу перед расправлением, но железо-галловые чернила относятся к случаям для профессионального консерватора. NPS также предупреждает, что сушка на воздухе скручивает, коробит и деформирует бумагу.
primaryGround: NPS Conserve O Gram 13/2: Flatten Folded or Rolled Paper; Introduction/cautions lines 24–38; process 66–85; drying 88–111. Many rolled/folded papers can be relaxed with carefully controlled humidification and then flattened. Objects with iron gall ink and objects in poor condition (large tears or embrittlement) require additional expertise and should be treated only by a professional conservator. The chamber method uses damp muslin, acrylic egg-crate and spun-polyester support, with periodic checks until the paper is damp, pliable and relaxed. Air-drying causes curl, warp and distortion; use the prescribed weighted blotter stack.

LOC Adjusted Water Washing of a 19th Century American Lithograph; Testing and Washing lines 32–56; treatment 57–68. LOC describes spot testing and adjusted wash solutions. Chelators remove otherwise insoluble salts; buffers maintain bath pH. A blotter wash used citric acid and tetrasodium borate; a later rinse used deionized water adjusted to pH 7.5 with saturated calcium hydroxide. Treatment aimed to improve legibility and strengthen weak, brittle paper.

LOC Mass Deacidification; Lines 30–32, 45–48. Adding alkaline compounds to acidic paper before embrittlement begins can extend useful life. Once paper is weakened, little can restore its original usability. A successful mass process raises pH to 6.8–10.4 and achieves at least 1.5% alkaline reserve.

CCI Notes 11/10: Encapsulation; Lines 29–54. Encapsulation is used to store and protect frequently handled paper artifacts. It allows handling and viewing through transparent material, protects against physical damage and is readily reversible. Polyester film should be transparent, strong, inert and durable. Electrostatic charge makes it unsuitable for friable media, backing-board attachments, cockled or warped objects, and items showing mould or insect infestation. Tape seals may be acidic and creep toward the artifact.

note0.literal: Промывка удаляет загрязнения и растворимые продукты; LOC проверяет чернила и пятна перед водной обработкой и подбирает состав ванны.
primaryGround: LOC Adjusted Water Washing of a 19th Century American Lithograph; Testing and Washing lines 32–56; treatment 57–68. LOC describes spot testing and adjusted wash solutions. Chelators remove otherwise insoluble salts; buffers maintain bath pH. A blotter wash used citric acid and tetrasodium borate; a later rinse used deionized water adjusted to pH 7.5 with saturated calcium hydroxide. Treatment aimed to improve legibility and strengthen weak, brittle paper.

primaryGround: NPS Conserve O Gram 13/2: Flatten Folded or Rolled Paper; Introduction/cautions lines 24–38; process 66–85; drying 88–111. Many rolled/folded papers can be relaxed with carefully controlled humidification and then flattened. Objects with iron gall ink and objects in poor condition (large tears or embrittlement) require additional expertise and should be treated only by a professional conservator. The chamber method uses damp muslin, acrylic egg-crate and spun-polyester support, with periodic checks until the paper is damp, pliable and relaxed. Air-drying causes curl, warp and distortion; use the prescribed weighted blotter stack.
